usefulness: Continuous torque supplies angular acceleration and finite spin-up/braking behavior that the present instantaneous impulse and prescribed visual rotation inputs do not express. A two-occurrence asymmetric-marker repair task is a coherent bounded physical advance. This is a qualitative development-priority judgment, not a measured authoring-benefit claim.
recommended_scope: Fixed-axis collinear first; no general time-varying-axis integration shortcut, compound body, contacts, joints or live engine physics.
physics_reasoning: For a fixed axis, signed omega is affine and signed angle quadratic on a constant-torque interval. For noncollinear omega0 and alpha, omega(t1) cross omega(t2) equals (t2-t1)*(omega0 cross alpha), so rotation generators at different times generally do not commute; exponentiating the integrated vector is not generally the trajectory.

pre_adoption_decisions.recommendation: Adopt fixed-axis collinear torque first if its representative utility review succeeds. Freeze how the axis is selected and persists through zero spin, opposing torque and reversal, when a new axis can begin, and whether each nonzero active torque or only the final net torque must align. Prefer a persistent signed scalar rotation state or another representation proven closed under canonical rounding. Do not reclassify axis alignment from a rounded public omega without a defined predicate.

A pure external torque changes angular state only. Preserve the translational trajectory anchor independently, including gravity and active COM forces. Do not let a rotational anchor update introduce extra rounding into an unchanged translation. Freeze zero-torque, cancelling overlap and same-net replacement controls.

Add angular-acceleration-aware recording bounds. For fixed-axis constant acceleration under ideal shortest-arc SLERP, the signed-angle interpolation defect is bounded by abs(alpha)*dt^2/8; actual interpolation, quaternion/time quantization and physical-state errors need their own predetermined margins. Retain the angular travel bound to prevent full-turn aliasing. Include reversal segments with identical endpoint orientations and nontrivial interior motion.

The asymmetric marker should be massless visual geometry or no_body visual descendants, with one body motion authority. The selected homogeneous sphere own mass/radius/inertia remain the physical model. Declare the torque an external couple with no added COM force or implied reaction/contact/joint model.

Reuse the existing Torque dimension (2,1,-2,0) and Inertia dimension (2,1,0,0). State the dedicated dynamics operation numerical SI-radian convention because ordinary Angle/AngularSpeed carry a distinct angle dimension. Do not silently alter generic dimensional arithmetic.

Freeze exact source activation/completion clocks, before/after meaning, final active torque summation, exposed net torque/alpha rounding and finite failures. Retain ordered impulse intermediate checks and whole-boundary rollback. Specify the precise domain refusal for an axis-changing impulse while torque is active and preserve older bindings unchanged.

source_basis.observed_basis: Current force trajectories share the inherited complete dynamic anchor and advance rotation at constant world omega.
Changed linear acceleration reanchors the complete state; unchanged acceleration retains the anchor.
Current force recorder explicitly assumes constant primitive angular contributions on each interval.
Current force interval checks translation chord error and angular travel; no angular-acceleration interpolation term exists.
Existing spin helper robustly handles constant-world angular velocity and preserves zero elapsed/spin anchors.
Angle is a distinct dimension; Torque and Inertia aliases already exist with their stated SI dimensions.
Existing sphere impulse scope uses own mass and isotropic inertia; visual descendants do not aggregate matter.
Existing finite force clocks, complete-boundary ordering, canonical sums, unchanged-anchor rules and valid-prefix behavior are adopted.

scope_of_acceptance: The draft already makes adoption, exact contract, independent preimplementation answers, predecessor preflight, publication/readback and all retained/full GOAL gates prerequisites. These findings refine that future contract review. This receipt adopts no torque syntax, profile, runtime or release promise.
